Outright weakness per vendor · fewest fails = best

The mandatory scope for this evaluation is the default critical-function set carried in the master config (the working top-20). A client revision isn’t edited here — it’s applied by reloading the master config at the start of an L2 session. Pending a formal per-requirement pass/fail, this view flags every domain at or below 2.00 Validated Capability as a capability fail. “Mandatory gaps” is deliberately avoided — mandatory status is a property of the requirement, not of a score.

Weighted SME Score Cards

Per-vendor headline: claim, validation, coverage, and where the two disagree

Each card decomposes a vendor's domain composites into the four Method-D measures. Capability is the average vendor claim across rows; Validation is the SME's average confidence in those claims; Coverage is the % of rows the SME could validate; Discrepancy counts rows where vendor and SME disagree by 2 or more. The headline Weighted SME Score rolls the SME (validation) scores into the strategic-weighted total used everywhere for ranking — each dimension's row-count-weighted SME average combined as D1 35% / D2 25% / D3 20% / D4 10% / D5 10% (D3 IS included). D3's vendor delivery effort is also surfaced separately as Delivery Effort Risk.

Dimension-level claim vs SME validation · ≥2.5 Fully · 1.5–2.4 Substantially · 0.5–1.4 Partially · <0.5 Not Met

How SME validation reshapes the vendor's self-scored ranking

SME Divergence — does the SME view change the ranking?

Two rankings per dimension: the vendors' self-scores vs the SMEs' independent validation

Vendors score their own delivery (capability: native / configuration / build / not met). SMEs independently score whether each requirement is actually met (validation) — the metric every headline ranking uses. This page compares the two: do the SMEs' findings change who wins versus taking the vendors' self-scores at face value? A rank flip marks a dimension where they do. Note that a requirement can be Fully Met (validation 4) even if delivered via configuration or build (capability < 4) — the route affects delivery risk / TCO, not the fulfilment score.

Material discrepancy = |vendor − SME| ≥ 2 · the diagnostic that justifies SME validation

Material Discrepancy Map

Where vendor claims and SME confidence disagree by 2 or more — the pattern matters

Each cell shows the count of rows where vendor and SME disagree by 2 points or more — these are the rows that change the conversation. Red intensity tracks over-claims (vendor higher than SME); blue intensity tracks conservative claims (SME higher than vendor). The pattern matters more than the total: discrepancies concentrated in one dimension signal a systematic issue; discrepancies spread thin across dimensions are routine calibration noise. D1 Fulfilment Route — how each vendor delivers their capability commitments

D1 (Functional Fit) rows only — vendor's self-certified route per requirement

Each vendor's D1 questionnaire labels every requirement with a fulfilment route: Delivered Natively (in the platform today), Configuration / Partner (via configuration or pre-integrated partner), New Build / Workaround (custom build, new partner, or manual process), or Not Met by mybank (outside the vendor's scope). Buy-mix = Native + Config; Build-mix = New Build + Not Met.

How much arrives in the box

In-box = Delivered Natively + Configuration/Partner · Bespoke = New Build / Workaround / Not Met · computed from imported routes

D3 Methodology Maturity — how each vendor builds the delivery

D3 (Implementation & Delivery) rows only — methodology bucketing per requirement

D3 carries a different vocabulary: Standard (standard methodology delivers), Tailoring (methodology established with tailoring required), Bespoke (bespoke or first-of-kind for mybank), or Not Addressed. Standard-mix is the parallel "off-the-shelf" signal for delivery — high standard% means the vendor builds it the same way every time.

Consistency check — claim vs delivery

Does the D1 capability story line up with the D3 delivery story?

A vendor claiming high buy% on D1 but low standard% on D3 is saying "the capability is off-the-shelf but the way we'll deliver it isn't" — that gap is the diagnostic. Threshold: divergence > 25 percentage points flags amber; > 40pp flags red.

Monte Carlo · robustness of the recommendation across 2000 plausible board configurations C.2
Ready · seat emphasis swept full-range, SQ lens jittered around your current position, L1 fixed
This is a structural diagnostic. Each sample re-draws every C-suite seat’s emphasis uniformly across its full range, and jitters the 13 SQ lens positions around your current lens (not across their entire range) — so robustness is measured in a neighbourhood of where you are now. The evidence baseline (L1) is held fixed; only the L2 lens varies, and effective SQ weights are clamped to their valid range. It answers: across plausible board compositions, how often does the recommendation hold, and what kind of board would flip it? Exact sampling parameters are shown with the results below.
Evidence jitter · robustness of the recommendation to plausible SME re-scoring (lens held fixed) C.3
Ready · SME scores re-drawn around the validated evidence, lens fixed
This is the complement to the board-configuration sweep above. It holds the boardroom lens fixed and instead perturbs the SME validation scores themselves — modelling the legitimate disagreement between evaluators looking at the same evidence — then reports how often the recommendation survives. It is hypothetical re-scoring, never the evidence: nothing is written back to L1, and the real scores are restored after every sample. It answers: holding the politics fixed, how robust is the recommendation to plausible re-scoring of the evidence?

Methodology & weighting (v1.0)

Ranking is on the Weighted SME Validation score — the SME requirement-fulfilment judgement (Fully / Substantially / Partially / Not Met), dimension-weighted (D1 35% · D2 25% · D3 20% · D4 10% · D5 10%) and requirement-count-weighted within a dimension. It reads the SME validation score only.

Delivery route (native / configuration / build) is a separate cost-risk signal (D3 / TCO) and never reduces a fulfilment score: a requirement Fully Met via configuration scores 4.

Weighting stack: dimension weights · within-dimension requirement count · role weights (lens) · seat coupling (gain 12.0, α=0, lens) · salience Critical 3 / Important 2 / Supporting 1 (strategic-alignment roll-up). Full note in the governance repository. mybank · CAKE / BinB / DIY.
